Using iMED, we evaluate 23 SOTA algorithms across tasks central to 3D
perception: rigid NVS, deformable (online & not) NVS, camera pose estima-
tion, feature matching, and depth estimation. Our analysis suggests that, under
this held-out-endoscope protocol, methods relying primarily on photometric su-
pervision degrade under physically independent viewpoints, while methods with
explicit geometric regularization are more robust across views. Depth super-
vision has representation-dependent effects, and large multi-domain foundation
models often transfer well to surgical imagery compared with surgical-only train-
ing or aggressive fine-tuning. We define train-on-one-endoscope, test-on-another
evaluation protocols that eliminate trajectory overlap and measure geometric
generalization across physically independent cameras, a standard in multi-view

pose estimation pipeline computing relative transformations between endoscopes
(Fig. 4). For each 5.7mm ArUco marker detected in both cameras, we estimate 6-
DOF poses using a Perspective-n-Point solver [27] with known marker geometry
and camera intrinsics. We aggregate observations across a sliding window and
compute rel. camera-to-camera transformations for commonly visible markers.
The full pipeline consists of five stages: (1)RANSAC Initialization and

to identify inlier observations based on angular and translational consistency
thresholds. We then refine the best hypothesis by minimizing bidirectional re-
projection error across all inlier marker corners using Levenberg-Marquardt op-
timization [33,40]. (2)Stereo Fusion:Each

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The train-on-one-endoscope, test-on-another protocol evaluates models on physically separate held-out cameras with independently derived reference poses and stereo disparity, providing a measurement outside the optimization loop.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are reported through quantitative metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, rotation error, inlier rate, and depth errors on held-out views from the physically distinct Endoscope 1, using calibrated reference poses.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The benchmarked models are optimized using their own pre-existing training objectives, including photometric rendering losses, depth priors, and matching objectives, on Endoscope 2 training data or external datasets.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the failure modes of purely photometric novel view synthesis under physically displaced held-out viewpoints and the transferability of foundation models are thoroughly supported by quantitative metrics across diverse tasks.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The authors benchmark 23 state-of-the-art methods across rigid and deformable novel view synthesis, pose estimation, feature matching, and monocular depth estimation, showing clear performance variations based on explicit geometric regularization and out-of-domain pre-training.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Models trained on one endoscope are tested against physically separate held-out cameras and evaluated on independently derived reference poses and stereo disparity.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective quantitative metrics (PSNR, SSIM, rotation error, inlier rate, and depth Abs Rel/RMSE) evaluated on held-out views from physically distinct Endoscope 1 using calibrated reference poses.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-existing public weights or standard task loss formulations (e.g., photometric L1/D-SSIM rendering losses, matching objectives) used to optimize the benchmarked models on Endoscope 2 training data or external datasets.

primary.limitations: The authors document key limitations including hand-guided motion in ex vivo sessions, the requirement of marker inpainting for dynamic sequences, and baseline/trocar field-of-view constraints inherent to surgical robotics.
primary.method_assessment: Data collection uses two synchronized stereo endoscopes (four 60 FPS video streams) with calibrated intrinsics, fiducial-based (ArUco) pose refinement with Levenberg-Marquardt optimization and uncertainty estimation, and sequence-level photometric matching.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript provides a rigorously constructed surgical dataset addressing a prominent methodological issue in surgical novel view synthesis (trajectory overfitting) and supports its claims with extensive benchmarking and thorough technical ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents iMED, a benchmark dataset of 340 synchronized multi-endoscope video sequences across ex vivo, postmortem, and live surgical settings, enabling train-on-one-endoscope, test-on-another geometric evaluation of 3D surgical perception tasks.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript provides a rigorously constructed surgical dataset addressing a prominent methodological issue in surgical novel view synthesis (trajectory overfitting) and supports its claims with extensive benchmarking and thorough technical ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors document key limitations including hand-guided motion in ex vivo sessions, the requirement of marker inpainting for dynamic sequences, and baseline/trocar field-of-view constraints inherent to surgical robotics.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

relation_to_agentic_memory.value: Segmentation task adjacent to detection; shares backbones and dense-prediction evaluation

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to computer-vision research based on screening evidence.
